status: All three prespecified matched pairs completed and passed the measurement audit; exploratory one-phone evidence, not a user-facing battery rating

pair1.conditions: Native battery state unplugged, LPM off, brightness 1.0 throughout; trace brightness 100; full trace thermal state Nominal. Native coarse battery gauge remained about 90%, which is not zero drain.
pair1.lifecycle: No stop; foreground at return. Native receipt retained in trace directory.
pair1.attachment: Initial PID lookup failed; same PID independently reconfirmed. One attachment retry confirmed recording before gate release. No workload retry/discard.

pair2.conditions: Unplugged, LPM off, native brightness 1.0 and trace brightness 100 throughout; all trace thermals Nominal. Coarse battery gauge changed from about 90% to 85%; not a calibrated app-only drain figure.
pair2.lifecycle: No stop; foreground at return. Native receipt retained.
pair2.attachment: Initial PID lookup failed; independently reconfirmed PID, one bounded attachment retry, then capture-ready release. No workload retry/discard.

pair3.conditions: Unplugged, LPM off, native brightness 1.0 and trace brightness 100 throughout; full thermal timeline Nominal. Native coarse battery gauge changed from about 85% to 80%.
pair3.lifecycle: No stop; foreground at return. Native receipt retained.
pair3.attachment: UDID/PID lookup failed twice; display-name and executable-name lookup also failed. Phone was unlocked, PID remained visible, and no leftover profiler existed. Selecting the independently verified device name with the same PID succeeded. This is a bounded workaround, not a proven root cause: time/reconnection may confound it. All failures retained in attachment-note.json; no workload restart or discard.
pair3.captureGate: Receipt arrived within the original 300-second gate; recording started before release and baseline began after 10.54 seconds of settling. Full phase coverage independently verified.

combined.latencyScope: Native generation only, excluding full hash/load/export/UI; 30-second reading pauses and idle padding are included in power workload windows, not generation latency.
combined.memoryScope: Different metrics; neither is a standalone RAM compatibility requirement.
combined.conditions: All native measured markers unplugged, LPM off, brightness 1.0; all full trace thermal timelines Nominal and trace brightness 100. Every pair started nominal with >=30% battery, with >120 seconds between measured pairs. All lifecycle receipts show no stop and foreground return.
combined.batteryGauge: Native coarse gauge moved approximately 90% →85% →80% across the whole instrumented session including setup/cooldown. This is retained separately and not reconciled to the profiler's integrated rates; do not treat it as calibrated app-only drain or infer answers per charge.

verification: 12 native runtime tests and nine Python analysis tests pass; signed build13 Release succeeds. All three physical matched phases exercised normal completion/capture timing. No forced 300-second overrun, charging switch or low-battery stop was induced in these runs; do not claim those physical edge cases were newly verified.
interpretation: Repeatable bounded whole-device rates were observed for this short-context paced workload on one iPhone at full brightness under wireless profiling. Baseline subtraction is a diagnostic difference, not exact app energy. This is not disconnected idle/sleep, optimized shipping UI/runtime, a general workload forecast or a battery-life promise. Unlabelled app-impact columns remain uninterpreted. Earlier partial capture and sustained-load thermal failure remain retained and unchanged.
recommendation: Keep a public battery-efficiency rating unmeasured for now. The three-pair experiment is complete; it need not block scoped General-chat integration. Disconnected real-use and integrated-app measurements remain separate future work if a battery rating is desired.
